newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Bank shares ease in quiet Lithuanian trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares ease in quiet Lithuanian trade.

text.p: Hermis Bank and Vilniaus Bank eased in quiet trade on Monday and dealers said they were hopeful that Lithuania's bearish bourse would soon pick up.
"Some shares look good now and their price is low, so things could pick up at any time," said Sigitas Petraitis of brokerage firm Vilfima.
Dealers cited Hermis Bank and Ekranas as blue chips that had room to grow.
Lithuanian Gas shares are suspended this week pending its shareholders' meeting and dealers were divided about its prospects.
The state-run gas firm's share price fell steeply last Tuesday and Wednesday before rallying a bit. It ended the week at 2.00 litas.
"If you look at Lithuanian Gas' numbers from 1996, things don't look very good, and there would seem to be no reason for its price to rise above 2.00 litas," said one dealer.
The company has admitted that its 1996 losses are at least 78 million litas.
But other dealers say the company's long-term prospects look good as the government gets serious about reforming the heavily indebted energy sector.
